claim: Locomotion dramatically enhances neural activity in the visual cortex (V1) of the mouse.
source: In previous work, we have shown that locomotion dramatically enhances neural activity in the visual cortex (V1) of the mouse (Niell and Stryker, 2010)
evidence: Supported by citation to Niell and Stryker, 2010

claim: The cortical circuit responsible for locomotion-induced enhancement of neural activity in visual cortex has been identified.
source: In previous work, we have shown that locomotion dramatically enhances neural activity in the visual cortex (V1) of the mouse (Niell and Stryker, 2010), identified the cortical circuit responsible for this enhancement (Fu et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to Fu et al., 2014

claim: Locomotion dramatically enhances adult plasticity.
source: shown that locomotion also dramatically enhances adult plasticity (Kaneko and Stryker, 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to Kaneko and Stryker, 2014

claim: The circuit responsible for enhancing neural activity in the visual cortex contains both vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) and somatostatin (SST) neurons.
source: The circuit that is responsible for enhancing neural activity in the visual cortex contains both vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) and somatostatin (SST) neurons (Fu et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fu et al., 2014

claim: The VIP-SST circuit is necessary for rapidly increasing V1 cortical responses following manipulation of visual experience in adult mice.
source: Optogenetic activation or genetic blockade of this circuit reveals that it is both necessary and sufficient for rapidly increasing V1 cortical responses following manipulation of visual experience in adult mice.
evidence: Supported by optogenetic activation and genetic blockade experiments described in the manuscript

claim: The VIP-SST circuit is sufficient for rapidly increasing V1 cortical responses following manipulation of visual experience in adult mice.
source: Optogenetic activation or genetic blockade of this circuit reveals that it is both necessary and sufficient for rapidly increasing V1 cortical responses following manipulation of visual experience in adult mice.
evidence: Supported by optogenetic activation and genetic blockade experiments described in the manuscript

claim: The VIP-SST circuit enhances plasticity directly, independent of locomotion and aerobic activity.
source: Here, we ask whether this VIP-SST circuit enhances plasticity directly, independent of locomotion and aerobic activity. Optogenetic activation or genetic blockade of this circuit reveals that it is both necessary and sufficient for rapidly increasing V1 cortical responses following manipulation of visual experience in adult mice.
evidence: The manuscript poses this question and provides experimental evidence through optogenetic manipulation

claim: A disinhibitory circuit regulates adult cortical plasticity.
source: These findings reveal a disinhibitory circuit that regulates adult cortical plasticity.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript

claim: The adult brain continues to learn.
source: The adult brain continues to learn and can recover from injury
evidence: Statement based on established scientific knowledge

source: The adult brain continues to learn and can recover from injury
